external_entities.name: member
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop and spend them on gift cards.

external_entities.name: member phone
external_entities.description: A member's phone running the mobile app and holding its refresh token.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone.

external_entities.name: member browser
external_entities.description: The browser used by a member to sign in and approve partner app consent.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

external_entities.name: partner app
external_entities.description: A web application run by another company on its own server, such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application members use to sign in and call the rewards API.
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

processes.name: authorization server
processes.description: The authorization server that authenticates members, handles authorization-code flows, issues tokens and manages partner consent.
processes.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
processes.notes: The member's sign-in is kept in a cookie for thirty days; nobody decided an idle timeout for it.

processes.name: rewards API
processes.description: The API that reads and writes the points ledger and processes points redemption.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

processes.name: support console
processes.description: A web application used to close a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.

data_stores.name: identity database
data_stores.description: Stores member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.

data_stores.name: points ledger
data_stores.description: Stores every member's points balance and every points transaction, including which client made each change.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: Stores every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: A member uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.
data_flows.data_description: Member interaction with the mobile app

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: The member phone runs and interacts with the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone.
data_flows.data_description: Mobile app requests and refresh-token data

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs a member in through the authorization server using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back
data_flows.data_description: Rewards API requests using an access token

data_flows.name: request token
data_flows.description: A partner app sends token requests containing its client secret in the request body.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.

data_flows.name: use browser
data_flows.description: A member uses a browser to sign in and approve partner app consent.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

data_flows.name: approve consent
data_flows.description: The browser connects to the authorization server sign-in page and consent screen.
data_flows.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen that lists the scopes

data_flows.name: return code
data_flows.description: The browser returns an authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.

data_flows.name: show points
data_flows.description: A partner app shows a member's points using the rewards API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points

data_flows.name: manage identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server reads and writes identity records, codes, tokens and consents.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_flows.data_description: Member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents

data_flows.name: read-write ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

data_flows.name: write logs
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes each received request, including headers, to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: take token
data_flows.description: The support console takes access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It takes access tokens from the same authorization server

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.

trust_boundaries.name: own cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud account where the system components and stores run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account, apart from the members' phones and the partner apps.

trust_boundaries.name: members' phones
trust_boundaries.description: Members' phones, which are outside the organisation's cloud account.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account, apart from the members' phones and the partner apps.

trust_boundaries.name: partner app servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers run by other companies for their partner applications.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API is internet-facing because it is served on the same public hostname as the support console.
assumptions.basis: The support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The support console is internet-facing because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The identity database is confidential because it contains member personal data, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.
assumptions.basis: The store contains member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger is confidential because it contains member-related financial and operating records.
assumptions.basis: The ledger holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store is confidential because its headers may contain credentials and tokens.
assumptions.basis: The rewards API writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.
